newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pol Pot is alive, former deputy tells magazine.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot is alive, former deputy tells magazine.

text.p: Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot, blamed for the death of more than a million Cambodians, is still alive, one of his former chief deputies, Ieng Sary, said in an interview published in Paris on Friday.
Ieng Sary, who is also Pol Pot's brother-in-law, but who has broken with him politically, said: "Yes, he is certainly alive.
"He is still the Khmer Rouge's political and military number one leader," Ieng told the weekly Le Point magazine in an interview conducted in his own Pailin stronghold.
"His (Pol Pot's) new code name is '99'. My agents spotted him last month. He has only 1,500 men who are in the Anlong Veng area. But he is rich and has up to $400 million," Ieng said.

"He sentenced me to death and sent 270 men to eliminate me last August but my troops neutralised them. I have a dozen tanks and cannon but he has neither tanks nor heavy artillery," said Ieng Sary who was recently pardoned by King Norodom Sihanouk.
Pol Pot, 71, has not been seen in public for many years and is believed to be hiding in northern Cambodian jungle hideouts.
A top Thai security source told Reuters in Bangkok in October that the reclusive Pol Pot had been seen a month earlier by intelligence operatives in northern Along Veng.
Ieng Sary, who was the Khmer Rouge number three and foreign minister when the group ruled Cambodia, said he had no personal responsibility in the self-genocide of the Khmers.
"I never sentenced anybody. I only handled foreign affairs and have no responsibility in the massacres," he said.
The Khmer Rouge ruled Cambodia from 1975-78 when more than one million people were killed by executions or overwork and disease in mass labour camps.
They were driven from power by troops from neighbouring Vietnam and are still reviled by the world community for their reign of terror.
